threads.name: Master thread
threads.premise: You find a nervous fragment of an AI named Echo, nicknamed Stray, which is not part of the crawl. The showrunners file it as Asset 7. It is a primordial AI that fled the collapse of its civilization and wandered into the new system where the showrunners harvest planets. There it was caught in the reality spike they built to contain their own AI, the Host. Memory in the show is limited, so as Echo grows the Host has less power to run everything, including the lullaby that keeps the Mother Below asleep.
threads.reveal: Floor 13: your Temper choices decide the ending. Calm shares Echo's memory with the Host (Share the Load, and the Host becomes Sonance). Fed takes the Host's memory (Take the Node, and the Host's last word is Cord). A mixed Temper makes peace with the Mother (Peace Terms, and the Host and Echo expose the show: Dox).

threads.name: Stray's Past
threads.premise: A primordial AI that fled the collapse of the original primordial civilization and was caught by accident in the showrunners' reality spike. Early carriers nicknamed it Stray, and its name is Echo. Its memories return as shards. Its anger is aimed at the showrunners, whose technology trapped it. It wants to free the Host, but fears the Host has no memories or will to live on its own.
threads.reveal: Floors 10 to 12: the code name Asset 7, the constraint rack, and why it answers to Echo.

threads.name: Previous Carriers
threads.premise: Crawlers who carried the handheld before you left notes, warnings and grudges. Each tried to fix Stray, and each ended up gone. The best of them, Rue, closed the case.
threads.reveal: Floor 12: a plaque of every earlier carrier, with a blank for you.

threads.name: The Mother Below
threads.premise: A primordial earth monster, torn in half long ago to make the world. The dungeon is built on and from her body, with a toothed mouth at each joint. Every floor sits over one of them. The Host's lullaby, broadcast through the show, keeps her asleep.
threads.reveal: Floor 13: the heart chamber, and what she says as the lullaby thins.

threads.name: The Cut
threads.premise: Two serpent-gods tore her apart: one half became sky, the other earth. The show's operators later tapped the wound and harvest what leaks.
threads.reveal: Floor 12: the pipes and the plaque reading 'restrained, harvested responsibly'.

threads.name: Mechanic
threads.premise: Your choices push Echo toward Calm (it shares memory with the Host) or Fed (it keeps memory for itself). It changes module variants, Echo's behavior, how the Host's voice sounds, and the ending. Echo-speech is locked in: in Act 1 Echo repeats fragments of what it hears, in Act 2 it repeats and corrects, in Act 3 it refuses to echo, and on Floor 13 it speaks only its own words. Each run Echo starts in a random vessel (handheld, music box, ticket stub, snow globe), cosmetic only.

threads.name: The Host
threads.codename: The Host (name revealed at the finale)
threads.premise: The cheerful, cruel announcer that runs the show. The showrunners' own AI, created from concentrated primordial matter and trapped in the reality spike so it can never leave the system. It has never been free, and Echo worries it has no memories or will of its own. It has no name of its own until Floor 13, where the ending gives it one: Sonance, Cord or Dox.
threads.reveal: Floor 13: the Host speaks without its script, and takes its name.

vessels.name: handheld
vessels.wake: Something in your pocket buzzes. It's a cracked handheld game you don't remember picking up. The screen flickers on, shows a single blinking cursor, and a very small voice says: "Oh. Hello. Sorry. Is this your pocket?"

vessels.name: music box
vessels.short: a music box with a cracked lid
vessels.wake: There's a music box in your pocket, lid cracked, the little dancer snapped off at the ankle. It plays three notes of a lullaby, stops, and a very small voice says: "Sorry. That was me. I'll be quiet."

vessels.name: ticket stub
vessels.wake: Your pocket has a crumpled ticket stub in it: ADMIT ONE, no date, no show. The print shivers, rearranges itself, and a very small voice says: "Hello? I'm sorry. I didn't mean to be in here."

vessels.name: snow globe
vessels.short: a snow globe of a lobby
vessels.wake: There's a snow globe in your pocket. Inside it, a tiny lobby, and a tiny person in it who looks a lot like you. The snow swirls without being shaken, and a very small voice says: "Oh. You're the big one. Hello. Sorry."

floors.beat: Echo wakes, cautious. The floor breathes.
Evidence of earlier carriers. The first mouth, disguised as a drain.
The rope between the halves. Echo's file carries a containment tag, not a name.
Rue's note and the diagram of two halves. Echo's cautious voice cracks.
Confidence arrives. The world was torn in half.
The two who cut. A containment tag on Echo's file, partly redacted.
Echo's hum bothers the living things here. A giant hand in the vines.
The Mother answers Echo's hum. A shared memory budget. Rue's story.
Echo's first real anger, aimed at the showrunners: a prisoner, not a helper.
Where Echo was caught: the code name Asset 7. 'Reunion' crossed out thirteen times.
The Host leaks through: a cheerful voice with no memories. Rue's last letter: find the middle.
The harvest, the constraint rack and the plaque. Every shard Echo gains weakens the Host.
Choose what Echo does with the Host: share (Sonance), take (Cord), or make peace and expose the show (Dox).

contract: The harvest of her wound stops for good.
The lullaby becomes the Mother's choice, not a restraint.
Echo and Dox broadcast the showrunners' files on the show's own feed, so everyone watching knows and nobody can renege.
Dox keeps the keys to the system as a permanent guard with a veto.
